name: Davenport Landing primitive campsites
coordinateNote: Entrance, parking or campsite coordinates from the November 12, 2026 research.
navigationNote: Drive to the listed entrance; follow the access description on arrival.
experience: Three primitive sites in floodplain forest above the Ocklawaha River at a former steamboat stop. No toilets, no water, no fee and no reservation. It is far from the springs: about 31 miles and 45 minutes north of Juniper, beyond Salt Springs.
access: First come, first served. Stay limit: Limit 15 people (5 per campsite); forest-wide 14 days in 30 Ocala WMA general gun season is Nov 14, 2026 - Jan 10, 2027 in the Pipeline, Hopkins Prairie and Lake Delancy units (Church Lake Unit on the far west edge: Nov 14-22 and Nov 28 - Dec 6). FWC 2026-27 brochure: 'During the general gun season, camping is prohibited, except in designated campgrounds and Juniper Prairie Wilderness.' Forest Service: 'Camping is allowed only in designated campsites during general gun season.' This is a designated campground, so it stays legal for the whole trip. Hunters will be on the surrounding forest roads; deer hunters must wear 500 sq in of fluorescent orange, and it is sensible to wear orange on trails outside the campground.

conditions.summary: The Forest Service lists the site as open and free (page last updated May 21, 2025). It is in the Lake Delancy hunting unit. The Forest Service lists it among its campsites, so it should count as a designated campsite during general gun season, but no source says so in those words: phone the Lake George Ranger District, 352-625-2520, before relying on it. (source dated read 2026-11-12)

camp.sedanNote: FR 74 (River Road) is improved native material rated 'suitable for passenger cars', but the last 0.4-mile spur to the landing (74-7.4, Reedy Bluff) is native sand rated high-clearance in Forest Service road data. A Dyrt reviewer in a van: 'Last 100 yards driving back in were very bumpy but no problem with our van.'
camp.carSleepingNote: No rule found either way; these are primitive tent sites reached by a short sand spur.
